children: Bank Negara Malaysia could pre-emptively raise its policy rate by 25 bps to 3.00% in March 2027, ahead of a projected pickup in core inflation, CIMB economists Chew Khai Yen and Michelle Chia say in a note. They previously expect BNM to keep rate at 2.75% through 3Q 2027. Budget measures could add 11.5 ringgit billion to household incomes, lifting consumption growth by 0.5 ppt and GDP growth by 0.2 ppt, they estimate. Stronger spending and rising wage costs could give businesses more scope to raise prices in 2H 2027 amid higher cost pressures stemming from the Middle East conflict and El Nino impact, they say. However, the hike could come as early as January if price pressures broaden, or could be delayed until May if domestic demand weakens. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
